s_e822e3cd: This is the final arithmetic applied after contacts, multipliers, bonuses, and penalties have been determined. Select the starting score and add operations in the same order as the published formula. Each step consumes the prior integer result and another supported integer variable or constant. Division must specify its integer rounding rule. Review the worked example after validation; it demonstrates the formula with sample values and is not a prediction of an entrant’s score. Example: 120 points × 8 multipliers + 10 bonus − 5 penalty = 965.
s_e8cb87e4: describes the fields sent and received for each contact, plus values declared once for the whole entry. It is the canonical vocabulary used by validation and scoring; the format mapping section connects these fields to names in uploaded Cabrillo or ADIF logs. WWROF’s standard Cabrillo QSO columns include sent and received RST and exchange positions. The sponsor defines the exchange contents; a serial is only one possible exchange. A new draft starts with a generic Contest exchange field that you can replace or expand to match the published rules. Field keys are stable references used by the system; labels are for display. Select a common field to prefill its key, label, type, and direction, or choose “Custom exchange field” for a contest-specific value. Choose “sent”, “received”, or “both” for contact exchanges, and “entry” for a single entry-level declaration. Mark a field required only if the sponsor requires it. Serial scope controls when a sent sequence number increments; enum values restrict accepted text to the listed choices.
